page.text:
Equipped with the core axioms of Zermelo--Fraenkel theory, we can now
define the canonical elementary constructors of mathematics.

The simplest non-trivial set formed from an existing entity $X$ is its
*singleton set*, denoted $\{X\}$, whose solitary member is $X$. The
existence of $\{X\}$ follows immediately from the Axiom of Pairing by
setting $Y = X$, so that $\{X\} = \{X, X\}$. It is conceptually vital to
maintain the ontological distinction between an element $X$ and its
singleton collection $\{X\}$: while $X \in \{X\}$, they are never
identical (indeed, the Axiom of Foundation forbids $X = \{X\}$ since that
would imply $X \in X$).
